approach: Add run/ci.rs: the CI branch name, a push and delete behind a small trait (Git-backed), the wait bound, and one helper `with_ci_source` that returns the source and the wait together. After admission, `check_and_verify` force-pushes the candidate to `athena/ci/<job id>`, only for a non-nested run whose origin is an https github.com URL, then calls `resolve` through that helper instead of `NoCi`. With no push the helper gives `NoCi` and a zero-pause single read, so a job with no GitHub remote never waits and the seam's pause override is not read. `routing::run_routed_recorded` returns the CI record; verification.rs turns it into a `ci-source` entry holding `verify::reuse_statement`. A resumed job rebuilds the record from only those resumed CheckRuns whose note carries the CI prefix and the candidate SHA and one common run address. `dispatch` deletes the branch once on every exit after the context exists. `[budget] ci_wait_s` (1500 s = 25 minutes) sets the wait. ci.yml gains the `athena/ci/**` push trigger and a corrected comment. Under cfg(test) the push is fail-closed: with no `ci_seam` installed nothing real is built or called. Every CI test installs `early_seam` (EarlyFake) and `ci_seam` through one `ci_run` helper. The guard test makes a real push visible without network: the test repo gets a repo-local `url.<bare>.pushInsteadOf=<github origin>`, so any real `git push origin` lands in a local bare repo that the test inspects, plus a cfg(test) counter of real-client constructions that must stay 0.

decisions.choice: Choose the source and the wait together in `with_ci_source(push: Option<&CiPush>, bound_s, f)`. With a push: `GhClient::new(runner, repo).ci_source(&push.branch)` and `ci_wait(bound_s)`. Without: `&NoCi` and `Wait { polls: 1, pause: ZERO }`. The no-push path never reads `bound_s` and never reads the seam's pause override (the override applies only inside `ci_wait`, which the no-push path does not call).
decisions.reason: `read_ci` keeps polling on `Ok(None)` and `NoCi` always returns it, so a 25-minute wait over `NoCi` would sleep in every job with no GitHub remote. One helper makes the wrong pairing impossible. The closure receives the `Wait`, so a unit test can read the chosen polls and pause directly (finding 3, 4).

rejected.why: Every job without a push would sleep 25 minutes before its local checks.

rejected.option: Pick the wait in run/mod.rs beside the call
rejected.why: Leaves two values that a later edit could pair wrongly.

The EarlyFake log is asserted to hold the early pull request's work-branch push, which shows the two pushes are separate.

The fake Runner panics on any argument list other than the runs GET or the jobs GET.

decisions.choice: Make a real push visible in the guard test (finding 1). The guard test uses a github origin `https://github.com/example/project.git`, installs `early_seam` only (no `ci_seam`), creates a bare repo in a tempdir and sets in the job repository `git config url.<bare path>.pushInsteadOf https://github.com/example/project.git`. `pushInsteadOf` is used, not `insteadOf`, because `git remote get-url origin` (what `github_repository` reads) expands only `insteadOf` and so still shows the github URL, while a real `git push origin` is rewritten to the bare repo. After `go` the test asserts: (a) `git for-each-ref refs/heads/athena/ci/` in the bare repo is empty; (b) the UI log has no 'warning:' line about the CI push; (c) `real_clients_built` is 0; (d) the check counter is 3. A positive control in the same test file drives the real `GitCiRemote` through the same redirect (no network) and asserts the ref lands in the bare repo, which proves the redirect catches a real push. Before the producer finishes it removes the fail-closed `return None` once, sees (a) and (c) fail, and restores it; the producer reports this in its notes.

decisions.choice: Resume rebuild (finding 2), stated exactly. `ci::record_from_resumed(&[CheckRun], sha) -> Option<CiRecord>` considers a run only if its note starts with the prefix `checks::runs_from_record` writes ('result reused from the CI run ', checks.rs:125) AND the note names the candidate SHA `sha`. Only those runs feed `steps` (name, passed, duration). All of them must name the same run address; if two addresses differ it returns None. A skipped-green check (routing.rs:210 writes a skipped note, not the CI note) and any locally run check are excluded, never counted as CI. A mixed set therefore yields a record built from only its CI runs; a set with no qualifying run, a wrong-SHA set or a conflicting-address set yields None. The record's SHA is `sha`; the address is parsed from the note. The unit test asserts each of these cases (all-CI gives Some with every step, mixed gives Some with only the CI steps, local-only None, wrong SHA None, two addresses None) and a pin test compares the prefix to the real output of `checks::runs_from_record`, so a wording change fails. The fresh-run record from `resolve` can list a skipped check that the resumed record omits; this only shortens the statement and the CHANGELOG notes it. Parsing the note is fragile text matching, accepted because the note is the only CI marker stored with the CheckRuns and the pin test guards it.
decisions.reason: The checks come from CI on resume but the record was only filled on a fresh run, so the verifier would read CI-derived results without a source statement. Criterion 5 requires the statement. A normal CI-sourced set can already be mixed, so the rule must say which runs count.

risks.risk: A job killed before close leaves `athena/ci/<job id>` on the remote.
risks.mitigation: The delete runs on every normal exit, including Err. The push is forced, so a leftover at another commit never blocks a retry (tested). Deleting a missing branch is Ok. No sweeper; the CHANGELOG says so.

risks.risk: Existing tests with a github origin (run_pin_tests.rs) reach the CI push and could make a real git push.
risks.mitigation: Under cfg(test) `push_ci_branch` returns None when no `ci_seam` is installed, before any real client is built. The guard test checks this against a local bare repo reached through pushInsteadOf, so the check does not depend on network failure; new tests always install both seams through `ci_run`.

risks.risk: The pushInsteadOf redirect in the guard test might not catch the push (for example if the push names the URL instead of `origin`), making the guard vacuous.
risks.mitigation: The positive control drives the real `GitCiRemote` through the same redirect and must see the ref land in the bare repo; if it does not, the control fails. The `real_clients_built` counter is an independent check.

risks.risk: Adding `ci_wait_s` to athena.toml changes the config hash, so queued readings are read again once.
risks.mitigation: The reread path handles it; the CHANGELOG mentions it.

risks.risk: Tests that reach `read_ci` with no usable reply would sleep for the real 25-minute bound.
risks.mitigation: They use `ci_wait_s = 0` or the zero-pause override; a Wait-values test covers 0 and 1500; one test counts 3 polls at 40 s.

risks.risk: A job with no push inherits the 25-minute wait over `NoCi`.
risks.mitigation: `with_ci_source` returns `NoCi` and the zero-pause single read whenever there is no push and never reads the bound or the override; a unit test reads the chosen Wait and the Runner call count is 0.

risks.risk: The rebuilt record on resume mislabels results or breaks if the note wording changes.
risks.mitigation: Only runs with the exact CI prefix, the candidate SHA and one shared address count; mixed sets use only the CI runs; a pin test ties the prefix to `checks::runs_from_record` output. The resumed statement may list fewer steps than a fresh one (skipped-green checks omitted); the CHANGELOG says so.

risks.risk: A candidate that changes a workflow file pushes a branch the token may refuse, or whose green run `resolve` ignores.
risks.mitigation: `resolve` ignores a green run when a workflow file changed; a refused push is one warning line and the local checks run.

risks.risk: The ci.yml cache is saved only from the default branch, so the first runs on athena/ci/** are cold and may exceed the wait.
risks.mitigation: On timeout `resolve` falls back to the local checks: correct, only slower. The bound is a config value.

risks.risk: The fake Runner's canned JSON could drift from what `pick_ci_run` and `parse_ci_run` expect.
risks.mitigation: The producer builds the JSON in the shape of gh/client.rs and gh/tests.rs; the green test fails if the shape is wrong.

Every github-origin test in ci_tests is built on `ci_run`, which asserts both seams are installed; the fake Runner panics on any gh call other than the runs and jobs GETs. Guard test `no_real_gh_or_push_is_attempted`: github origin, `early_seam` only, no `ci_seam`, a bare repo plus repo-local `url.<bare>.pushInsteadOf=<origin>` so a real push would land in the bare repo. A control test drives the real `GitCiRemote` through the same redirect and shows the ref lands, and a second real-bare-repo test pushes over a leftover branch at another commit.
demonstrations.observes: Each outcome logs exactly [push, delete] on `athena/ci/<job id>`, with the candidate record existing at push time; the reread path shows one push and one delete. Guard test: the bare repo has no `refs/heads/athena/ci/*`, the UI log has no 'warning:' line about the CI push, `real_clients_built` is 0, the counter is 3, and EarlyFake received only the early pull request's calls. Control and leftover tests: the forced push succeeds, `ls-remote` shows the new commit, delete removes it and a second delete is Ok. `cargo test -p athena-core` also runs the existing github-origin tests (run_pin_tests.rs), which push nothing for CI.
demonstrations.fails_without: No delete: the log lacks it. Delete in the wrong place: the reread case shows two or none. Push before admission: the probe finds no candidate record. Non-forced push: the leftover test fails. With the fail-closed rule removed, the guard test breaks on two assertions with no network involved: the real `git push origin` is redirected into the bare repo so `refs/heads/athena/ci/<id>` exists, and `real_clients_built` is 1. The producer removes the rule once to see this and restores it.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` (exists). Recording remote and gh::Runner fake via `ci_seam::install` (step 3; fakes written in step 10). `early_seam` with EarlyFake exists. The fail-closed rule and the `real_clients_built` counter are added in steps 3 and 5. `GitCiRemote` runs production `Git::force_push_branch` and `delete_remote_branch` (step 1) over a tempdir bare repo, with git config set through the repo's own `git config`. Reread setup follows run/pin.rs and run_pin_tests.rs.

demonstrations.method: Install the fakes and the check_seam counter with `ci_wait_s = 1500` (no pause override is installed, and the no-push path would ignore one). Run `go` to a verified outcome three times: no origin; a local-path origin containing github.com; an ssh origin. A unit test calls `with_ci_source(None, 1500, |src, wait| ..)` and reads the Wait.
demonstrations.observes: For each origin form the remote fake's log is empty, the Runner fake's call count is 0, the counter is 3, and the job takes under 20 s as a loose backstop. The unit test sees polls 1 and pause ZERO, so no wait ran.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing github guard: push, delete and runs query appear in the logs. A long wait over `NoCi`: the unit test sees polls above 1 or a nonzero pause, and the backstop fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` (exists). The guard is the real `Athena::github_repository` (step 4, from `https_github_repository`, early.rs:305). The `with_ci_source` no-push path is production code (step 5). ci_seam and early_seam fakes only record (steps 3 and 10); `check_seam` exists.

demonstrations.method: Resume at the verifier stage with CI-sourced checks, following `low_disk_before_the_verifier_holds_the_job_and_a_retry_resumes_it` (run/tests.rs:1605). First `go` with a green push run and a disk hold, so the checks are recorded with 'result reused from the CI run' notes. Then retry: ci_seam is installed but the second `go` must not push or call `resolve` again. A unit test of `ci::record_from_resumed` covers all-CI, mixed (CI plus skipped plus local), local-only, wrong SHA and two differing addresses, and a pin test compares the note prefix to `checks::runs_from_record` output.
demonstrations.observes: The resumed verifier's brief-verifier.md holds the `ci-source` entry with the `verify::reuse_statement` text naming the CI run address and the candidate SHA. The counter is 0 across both runs; the remote log shows one push. Mixed set: Some with only the CI steps; local-only, wrong-SHA and conflicting-address: None, so no statement.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rebuild `Checked.ci_record` is None on resume and the brief has no statement. Building steps from every run fails the mixed-set assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` twice (resume as in run/tests.rs:1605, using `test_support::low_once_verifying`, exists). ci_seam and early_seam as above. `record_from_resumed` is added in step 5 and used in step 7; it is real code, not faked.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gates over the whole workspace. `cargo test --locked` carries the new run::ci_tests, the athena-git push and delete tests, the athena-data config tests, the routing unit test and the xtask policy and budget tests.

demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0 and the summary shows the new ci_tests passing. The existing github-origin tests in run_pin_tests.rs still pass with no network.
demonstrations.fails_without: Unformatted files fail fmt. Dead code (an unused `NoCi` import or unused seam) fails clippy -D warnings. A missing push, resolve call, delete, fallback or config default fails ci_tests or the config tests. Text that breaks the boundary scan fails the xtask tests.
demonstrations.seam: The production entry points are the cargo commands. Inside `cargo test` the behavior is driven through `Athena::go` with the `ci_seam` and `early_seam` fakes and the existing `check_seam`; the fakes only record calls and return canned runs.

open_questions: Does the closing reason of a failed job carry judge's `check <name> failed` text? The red test asserts it; if closing code rewrites reasons the producer adjusts the assertion, not the code.

The JSON shape of the runs and jobs replies and the aggregate job constant (`CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`) were not read this round beyond the name; the producer copies them from gh/client.rs and gh/tests.rs (read only).

Does `athena_git::Git` push through the remote name `origin`, so that `pushInsteadOf` redirects it? I did not read the push code; the positive control test settles it, and the producer switches the redirect form if it does not.
`CiRecord` built on resume has `duration_s` summed from the CI-run CheckRuns' `duration` Quantity; the producer reads the Quantity accessor in athena-data. The sum only changes the printed seconds.

`routing::route` sets `reuse` only for a non-Build kind whose checks cover fmt, clippy and test; the producer reads it and installs the athena.toml checks in the ci tests if the harness defaults do not cover them.

The reuse statement goes to the verifier as an extra `ci-source` check entry because `VerifierInputs` is in athena-context, not a deliverable. Is that acceptable, or should the brief type gain a field in a later job?
